newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia warns 1996/97 migrant places running out.
newsitem.headline: Australia warns 1996/97 migrant places running out.

text.p: Australia warned on Monday it would run out of places for immigrants in several key categories within the next few months.
"The number of visas available in some immigration categories will be reached in a matter of weeks," Immigration Minister Philip Ruddock said in a statement.
"In the affected categories, no more visas will be granted for people to come to Australia until places become available next financial year," Ruddock said.
The government expected to reach the limits on visas in seven categories, including the independent category and various family groups, between the end of this month and May.
Ruddock last week began an annual round of community consultations used to help set the total immigration intake for the fiscal year to June 30, 1998.
The conservative Liberal-National government cut migrant numbers soon after ousting the Labor party in March, 1996.
It set a limit of 74,000 migrants for 1996/97, compared with the 82,500 set by Labor in 1995/96. The figures do not include about 13,000 places under the refugee and humanitarian programmes.
